title: Pathway Rotation: Digital Marketing
description: Week 6 is the Digital Marketing rotation: five weeks of self-marketing becomes deliberate, data-driven strategy. Participants craft a positioning statement and deconstruct high-performing content (hook, structure, CTA); interpret impressions and engagement on their weeks 1-5 posts, identifying what actually generated conversations; and design a simple campaign — audience, message, channel, cadence, metric — supporting Demo Day turnout. Weekly milestone: two-week content calendar built; best-performing post analysis delivered.
notes: Weekly milestone: two-week content calendar built; best-performing post analysis delivered.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1200-1800 words each, supporting a full week of live instructor-led practice
learning_objectives: Craft a positioning statement and deconstruct high-performing content into hook, structure, and CTA
Interpret impressions and engagement on real posts and identify what generated conversations
Design a simple campaign with audience, message, channel, cadence, and metric

lessons.title: Positioning & Content Strategy
objectives: Craft a positioning statement and deconstruct high-performing content into hook, structure, and CTA
Identify which element of a post drives attention, retention, and response

lessons.title: Analytics: Reading Your Own Data
objectives: Interpret impressions and engagement on real posts and identify what generated conversations
Attribute booked conversations to the content that caused them, resisting vanity metrics

lessons.title: Campaign Thinking
objectives: Design a simple campaign with audience, message, channel, cadence, and metric
Build a two-week content calendar supporting Demo Day turnout

sequencing_rationale: Week 6 is the Digital Marketing rotation: five weeks of self-marketing becomes deliberate strategy. Positioning and content deconstruction first, analytics second because participants now read their own weeks 1-5 post data, campaign design last because it synthesizes both into a plan supporting Demo Day turnout. Scope assumption: LinkedIn is the platform of record (it is where the program's posting happened); analytics stay platform-level, not paid-media.
